thread.title: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Lags, This Dow Stock Just Broke Out; When To Buy This Hot Bitcoin ETF

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Lags, This Dow Stock Just Broke Out; When To Buy This Hot Bitcoin ETF
text:
Stocks continued to shine on the third day of trading in 2018, and this time the Nasdaq lagged.
X Following gains of 1.5% and 0.8% on Tuesday and Wednesday, the tech-rich Nasdaq composite rallied 0.2% by day's end, backing off intraday highs in a rather tight trading session. Yet the leading index of 2017 (up more than 28% that year) still looks poised to hold firmly above the 7000 level in its first week of trading in 2018.
Defensive stocks continued to struggle. The Dow utility average, losing more than 1% on both Tuesday and Wednesday, fell another 0.8% on Thursday. The Dow transports added 0.3% and stands as a current leader among sector indexes since Jan. 1, up more than 2%.
Meanwhile, DowDuPont ( DWDP ) is giving large-cap investors a chance to time their new buy wisely as the chemicals giant broke out Thursday, rising out of a nearly 10-week flat base that shows a 73.95 buy point. Shares rose 2.1% to 74.60, helping the  s rise 0.6%. The S&P 500 is up 0.4%.
For a flat base, simply add 10 cents to the base's left-side high, or in DowDuPont's case, 73.85. DowDuPont corrected less than 8% within the base from intraday high to low, falling nicely within the maximum 15% decline threshold.
Volume in DowDuPont, a fundamentals turnaround play not too unlike Apple 's ( AAPL ) situation in 2016-2017, is running mildly above average. For a big or megacap stock, you'd prefer to see volume run 40% above the 50-day average or higher. However, in some cases, huge turnover doesn't come in until days or even weeks after the breakout itself.
Also notice on a daily chart how turnover has definitely heated up compared with the dull volume days during the last two weeks of December.
Analysts see DowDuPont's earnings up just 1% in 2017 to $3.22 a share, but then surge 25% to $4.03 a share, which would be the highest earnings since at least 2008. Total sales rose 36% in 2016 to $66.18 billion, and are seen gaining 18% in 2017 to $78.07 billion and up 7% to $83.48 billion this year.
DowDuPont has grown sales in each of the past seven quarters. The increases range from 8% to 46%.
The   average component has 2.34 billion shares outstanding and a market value of $174 billion.
The Street sees earnings slipping 33% to 66 cents a share in the fourth quarter of 2017, despite revenue rising 49% to $19.43 billion. There may be some restructuring expenses hitting the bottom line following a historic merger between Dow Chemical and DuPont. The company has been cutting jobs and closing facilities as part of a $3 billion savings plan.
However, DowDuPont's earnings are expected to bounce back the next quarter, rising 20% to $1.21 a share in the first quarter of 2018 on an 8% hike in sales to $22.17 billion.
Elsewhere the highflying Bitcoin-tracking Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) is cooling its heels after stupendous gains in December. The ETF fell just 2.2% to 2,204 in ultralight trade. Average volume has recently expanded to 133,000 shares, so the dollar volume is ample for most traders.
At this point, following a hyperbolic run last month and a elevatorlike plunge over just four sessions, quiet trading is a welcome change. But at the current price level, the risk of losing money on a new buy is likely higher than normal. Why? Bitcoin Investment has not corrected long enough to produce a genuine new chart pattern that can maximize short-term gain and minimize losses.
Over the next several weeks, keep tracking the price movement. Does it hold above its fast-rising 50-day moving average? Will it form a bullish new base such as a cup or double bottom? Or do big sellers come in strong again? Only time will tell.
Some commentators believe the strength of Bitcoin is bullish for gold. Gold-related ETFs are doing well so far this year.
The SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) investment trust rose more than 0.5% to 125.46 in turnover boosting 10% above usual levels. A new base has been forming since the large-cap ETF topped at 128.32 in September. SPDR Gold is now less than 3% below that peak.
The current base has elements of a double bottom, which would give a 124.07 entry, 10 cents above the Oct. 16 middle peak of 123.97.
Airlines have been rising in recent months, but strength in crude oil futures lately may serve as a stiff headwind. American Airlines ( AAL ) tried to break out of an 11-week cup with handle that features a 53.57 buy point. But shares, after hitting as high as 54.40 intraday, shaved its gain to less than 0.7% at 52.68. Plus, volume is limp.
Southwest Air ( LUV ), part of IBD Leaderboard , is down slightly. At 64.70, it's extended from a proper buy point, after having broken out past 59.99 in a large cup with handle.
According to IBD Stock Checkup , Southwest has one of the best Composite Ratings among the U.S. companies within IBD's Transport-Airline industry group at 81 on a scale of 1 to 99.
The Dow transportation average rallied 0.4%. At 10,863, the sector index is up nearly 2.4% since Jan. 1.
